title: Fix unverifiable Android App Link intent-filters for sign-in/invite deep links (AndroidManifest.xml)
rule: Tier-2 correctness (no numbered rule ID; auth/deep-link infra consistency)
why: Live verification (2026-07-03): https://torah-study-tracker.firebaseapp.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json returns HTTP 404, the domain root '/' returns HTTP 404, and '/sign-in' returns HTTP 404 — only Firebase's built-in /__/auth/action handler responds. Neither firebase.json (root or learning_tracker/) declares a "hosting" block, so nothing can ever serve assetlinks.json or these custom paths as currently configured. Android only honors autoVerify="true" intent-filters after validating that file, so it never marks the app as the verified handler for /sign-in or /invite. A parent tapping 'finish sign-in' in their email, or a tutor tapping an invite link (PP-7 wave-B, AndroidManifest.xml:57), gets sent to the system browser instead of the app — which then also 404s, since no Hosting deployment serves those paths either. Both flows dead-end on an error page.
recommendation: Either deploy Firebase Hosting with a committed .well-known/assetlinks.json (declaring package name + release SHA-256 cert fingerprint) and add the "hosting" block to firebase.json in the same change, or drop the autoVerify/pathPrefix App Links approach for a mechanism that doesn't need host-level verification. Add a deploy/CI smoke check that curls the assetlinks URL and fails the pipeline on non-200.
acceptance_criteria: curl -f https://torah-study-tracker.firebaseapp.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json returns 200 with correct package_name/sha256_cert_fingerprints, wired into a deploy or CI check that fails the pipeline on regression.
Tapping the sign-in continuation link and a tutor-invite link on a real or emulated Android device opens the app directly, not the browser or a 404 page.
